_comment: PER-MODEL-LOADOUTS (Stage 3). 10e core: every model in a unit is equipped with its own wargear (weapons), and a model can only make attacks with weapons it is equipped with. A unit's models may carry different weapons (a squad's special-weapon model, a sergeant's pistol-and-power-fist, a single-model Knight's specific gun rack). When a model is destroyed it is removed and can no longer make any attacks, so its weapons are lost from the unit's firepower. SwegHammer historically collapsed a whole squad into ONE averaged synthetic weapon shared by every model-Unit, and single-model units historically over-collected mutually-exclusive weapon options and fired them all. Stage 3 (env-gated SWEG_PERMODEL) instantiates one Unit per model from the BSData per-model loadout, so each model fires only the weapons it actually carries, a special weapon is lost when its model dies, and a single-model unit fires only its real equipped weapons (alt-mode mutual exclusivity and pistol exclusivity are still enforced by the existing simulator.multi_profile_weapon_selection / simulator.pistol_exclusivity picker). Damage stays at the expected-value mean at this stage; per-weapon dice rolling is a later stage. This is a faithful representation change, not a new buff: the per-model fields are the same BSData stats already carried on the aggregate, just attributed to the model that owns them.

simulator.per_model_loadouts.quoted_text: Each time a model makes an attack, you must use one of the weapons it is equipped with. ... A weapon's profile tells you ... Each model is equipped with the weapons shown on its unit's datasheet.
simulator.per_model_loadouts.trigger: a model in a unit makes an attack, or a model is destroyed
simulator.per_model_loadouts.effect: each model uses only the weapons it is equipped with, so a unit's distinct model types fire their own real loadouts (special-weapon model, sergeant, single-model gun rack) rather than one shared squad average, and a destroyed model's weapons are removed from the unit's firepower; alt-mode and pistol exclusivity are still enforced per the existing multi-profile picker

simulator.override_melee_precedence.rule_name: Weapons / Making Attacks — override precedence for the per-model loadout rebuild
simulator.override_melee_precedence.quoted_text: Each time a model makes an attack, you must use one of the weapons it is equipped with. ... Each model is equipped with the weapons shown on its unit's datasheet.
simulator.override_melee_precedence.trigger: SWEG_OVERRIDE_MELEE_PRECEDENCE default-off ('1' opts in, unset/'0' is byte-identical); code.army.Army._add_squad_per_model builds each per-model UnitProfile via dataclasses.replace(profile, **weapon_fields), where weapon_fields comes from code.units._loadout_entry_to_weapon_fields(entry).
simulator.override_melee_precedence.effect: DATA-CORRECTNESS FIX, companion to simulator.per_model_loadouts. _loadout_entry_to_weapon_fields unconditionally rebuilds extra_melee_profiles and extra_ranged_profiles on every per-model Unit straight from the mapper's model_loadouts data, which silently discards a hand correction in data/overrides.json that explicitly set one of those two fields to fix a mapper mis-parse of a unit's real datasheet weapon list (for example the Chaos Knights Knight Despoiler's second Reaper chainsword strike profile, or the Knight Tyrant's hand-corrected extra_ranged_profiles list). The override still merged correctly into the aggregate UNIT_CATALOG-level UnitProfile, but every per-model Unit the army actually fired with reverted to the mapper's uncorrected version, so the hand fix was inert in every simulated battle. When the gate is on, code.army._add_squad_per_model consults the new UnitProfile.override_field_names marker (populated in code.bsdata.loader._apply_override from the raw overrides.json entry, before the codex-corrections and calibrated-points layers are merged in) and leaves any field it names untouched during the rebuild, so dataclasses.replace keeps the aggregate's override-derived value instead of overwriting it. A blast-radius audit of data/overrides.json found 33 units carrying an extra_melee_profiles or extra_ranged_profiles hand override with a resolved per-model loadout; 26 of them were actively affected (the hand-set value differed from what the per-model rebuild produced) before this fix. Off path (SWEG_OVERRIDE_MELEE_PRECEDENCE unset or '0') restores the unconditional rebuild byte-identically.
